title: Cold rebuild: Match the bracket
summary: Rebuild Match the bracket from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Match the bracket** in *Lines, characters and jumps*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The line is `name = "value"` with the cursor on `n`. Which keys put the cursor on the `e` that ends `value`?
steps.explain: `$` reaches the closing quote and `h` steps back one. Three `e`s stop at `name`, `=`, then the opening quote; two `f"` land on the closing quote.

steps.title: Rebuild Match the bracket cold
prompt: Write `int Percent(string line, int col)` modelling `%` on one line:
- find the first bracket among `()[]{}` at or after `col`; if there is none, return `col`.
- jump to its match, counting nesting of the **same** bracket type (`(` and `)` only count each other). Opening brackets search right, closing ones search left.
- if there is no match, return `col`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
